title: Match real and wrong constituent pairs at the same glyph frequency and position
statement: Calibrate the Matlach, Janečková and Dostál eight-rule triplet score with matched real and wrong known constituents in pinned English, Latin and Italian text. A target AB and another pair AD share the first component. Replace matched, separated occurrences by distinct symbols X and Z. In the resulting text compare X with Z as candidates for the same fixed components AB. Match word boundary positions and, in a second condition, the exact previous glyph.
check: Repeat the recorded contrasts and score both printed and stated-rule readings at the published weights and 5% rank threshold. Verify that matching immediate left contexts leaves both candidate scores equal despite distinct right contexts. Test a separately fitted direct-emission line chain and compare manuscript rank sensitivity to the single-context Pearson convention.

sources.article: Vladimír Matlach, Barbora Anna Janečková and Daniel Dostál (2022), The Voynich manuscript: Symbol roles revisited, Detecting the ligatures and Figure 6. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0260948
sources.previous_experiment: experiments/K-031-open-2/fleet-sol/step.json. This report extends the earlier natural and stationary whole-copy checks with frequency-and-position-matched competitors and identical-incidence controls.

methods.natural_text: Use separate vs.refcorpus train_text and control_text block sets for English, Latin and Italian. Take up to 40,000 characters before the final partial word with single spaces. Fix first and second pairs as th/to and ea/er, en/es and pa/pe, ch/co and de/di respectively. For each word-position class shuffle the two occurrence lists with seed 9141 or 9142, attempt pairs in that order, and discard any pair whose edits overlap or touch previously accepted edits or one another. Shuffle accepted pairs with the same generator. Take 25%, 50% or 100% of the accepted pool, rounding down. Full-pool coverage of all original target occurrences has median 83.9% for positions only and 64.1% when the immediate previous glyph also matches. X and Z have exactly the same counts and no self-adjacent occurrences.
methods.loss: Use the joint adjacency matrix with spaces and zero edges below 0.2% of either their row or column. Rank all ordered triplets whose non-space glyphs exceed the published support ratio 500/229431, excluding a candidate used as its own component, and include ties in the percentile. Hold weights 1,100,1,1,100,1,1,10. Literal mode follows printed Rule 3 (shared contexts) and Rule 6 ((1−min)/max). Prose-based mode uses unshared contexts for Rule 3 and 1−min/max for Rule 6, following the prior experiment’s alternative. The paper describes a zero loss for empty contexts. Our primary analysis also uses zero for a singleton left context, where Pearson is undefined. For the public manuscript we rerun with a loss of one for that singleton. Zero correlation is assigned if either realized vector has zero variance with at least two contexts.
methods.exact_surrogates: For the first natural contrast of each language’s control block at full matched coverage, shuffle the directed adjacency list of every glyph and reconstruct an Euler trail beginning with the original first glyph. The output draws individual glyphs from the fixed edge multiset and never does a pair replacement during generation. It is conditioned on the positive sample’s observed incidence matrix and preserves the entire unigram and adjacent-pair counts by construction. This control tests identifiability from those inputs, not the plausibility of its whole-text generator.
methods.stationary_lines: Fit an initial-glyph distribution and one shared internal character transition table on public practice training paragraph lines for each edition. Use only raw certain ASCII EVA words with single spacing. Independently emit the public evaluation line lengths with the fixed table and seeds 7810–7815, disallowing a trailing space so the scoring stream contains one separator between lines. No pair-to-symbol rule is used. Score the two real public partitions separately in ZL and Takahashi under the same preprocessing.

findings: For word-position matching only at full matched coverage, eight comparisons met the frequency threshold. The wrong constituents have a better loss in six, while the true ones have a better loss in two. This is 3 of 4 wrong wins in training and 3 of 4 in the separate control blocks. Both alternatives fall within the published 5% cutoff in four cases. At half coverage the wrong option wins 5 of 7 eligible trials, and neither option passes the cutoff in any eligible case.

All 13 eligible comparisons in the exact-left condition tie across the three replacement fractions. All 36 exact-left trials, including below-support cases, have differing right-context incidence counts. The loss depends on the candidate’s left contexts, frequency and self-adjacency. These are shared by X and Z, while the candidate components and their directed pair frequency are fixed. The score therefore ties even when the right contexts differ.

The three shuffled Euler trails change 91.4–92.3% of positions while preserving every loss, over 9,702, 9,702 and 11,132 eligible triplets respectively. This invariance follows from the use of unigram and adjacent-pair counts as the only numerical inputs.

In twelve direct-emission stationary line simulations, m with i,d falls in the best 5% in all twelve, and q with i,e in eight. Under both Rule 3/6 conventions, those results hold without combining any symbols.

For q with i,e, the rarer glyph contributes just one realized incoming context after trimming in each public evaluation edition. The prose-based rank moves from 4.41% to 9.63% in ZL and from 4.39% to 9.86% in Takahashi when assigning loss one instead of zero to that undefined singleton correlation. This crosses the paper’s cutoff with the text and all other rules fixed.

scan.locus: f20v.1, first word and first mark
scan.observation: Matches the leftmost f example in Figure 6. The tall faint upright reaches the baseline. There are two long strokes to the right, a high loop and a short hooked branch on the left. The lower right stroke fades before a return curve. ZL and Takahashi both read the opening word as faiis under split-comma tokenization. The image leaves stroke order and the status of a curve as a separately written component unresolved.

interpretation: A low triplet percentile can arise for an incorrect constituent pair or for directly generated glyphs. This calibration addresses statistical specificity. Independent visual evidence can still support a ligature hypothesis. Most partial fusions lack frequency support, and these contrasts share a first component by design, so the results do not estimate error rates over every possible ligature.

reproduction.instructions: Extract the script to a scratch location and run PYTHONPATH=. python3 /path/voynich_triplet_specificity.py from the repository root with pinned inputs fetched. The two manuscript partitions used are the public practice training and evaluation pages.
